panels.title: Quantized encoder energy
panels.subtitle: Encoder energy · 200 inference runs · external power monitor
panels.finding: The Small encoder uses 3.55–4.92 mJ per inference, below the Base encoder on every measured device.

takeaways: New vocabularies: add labeled support clips without retraining the encoder.
Small encoder: lower latency and energy on all three measured devices.

notes: All 12 displayed values were checked visually against Table 1. Small is TinyNet-E and Base is EfficientNet-v2 Medium. Quantized Small ranges are exact extrema of the three displayed device rows.
Mean costs average 200 inference runs and include the encoder only. They exclude log-mel preprocessing and prototype classification; do not describe them as end-to-end latency or battery use.
The table does not pair quantized runtime with a matching recognition-accuracy result. No recognition score is inferred from a figure or transferred from a non-quantized evaluation.

The concise recognition takeaway is qualitative: held-out vocabulary and unseen-language evaluation uses closed-set few-shot episodes. FLEURS experiments are 3-, 5- or 10-way episodes, not 102-way identification.
Full-precision rows remain in the insight data but are omitted to compare the same model format across devices. No disputed prose speedup factors are repeated. No insight-data correction was needed.
